featured_reviews.name: Hitesh Harisinghani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Revisited this little seafood spot after 6–7 years and it felt like meeting an old friend who hasn’t changed one bit, in the best way possible.
The space is still compact (barely 4-5 tables, seating around 18–20 people), but the addition of A/C is a welcome upgrade.

The menu is limited, but honestly, you’re here for the thalis—and they absolutely deliver. The prawns thali was the highlight: 2 chapatis, rice, a soulful fish curry, 7–8 small fried prawns, jawla, salad, cabbage, and sol kadi. Everything was simple, balanced, and deeply satisfying. The curry stood out—rich, comforting, and packed with flavour—while the sol kadi was fresh and refreshingly light.

The chicken thali didn’t lag behind either. The curry was delicious, paired perfectly with the usual sides—rice, chapati, salad, and sol kadi—making it a wholesome, no-fuss meal.

We also tried the bombil fry, which came perfectly crispy and fresh—exactly how it should be.

At just ₹760 for two, this place is unbelievably economical. Add to that the warm, friendly staff, and you’ve got yourself a true hidden gem in Juhu.

featured_reviews.name: Sunil D'Silva
featured_reviews.review_text: Goa Bhavan is a quaint little canteen with very limited seating, but that’s exactly its charm. It feels less like a restaurant and more like a warm local Goan home kitchen. The staff serve with genuine smiles and even check if you’d like a little top-up of food — a lovely touch that makes you feel cared for. The food is simple, fresh, tasty, and unbelievably value for money. Far from fancy, but full of heart. Perfect spot for a quiet, homely seafood meal served with warmth and authenticity.

featured_reviews.name: Floyd Pinto
featured_reviews.review_text:

Loved their fish thali and the goan prawn masala

featured_reviews.name: chaturved falari
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving authentic Goan seafood that takes you straight to the beaches of Goa, Goa Bhavan in Juhu is a hidden gem you cannot miss! From the moment I walked in, the homely vibe and subtle aroma of freshly prepared seafood set the tone for an amazing experience.

The Prawns chilly was a delightful explosion of flavors—perfectly marinated with tangy masala that hit all the right notes. The Pomfret Thali was the star of the show—succulent fish fried to perfection, accompanied by a medley of traditional Goan sides that balanced the spices and textures beautifully.

I also tried the Bombil Fry and Surmay Fry, both incredibly crispy and seasoned just right, preserving the natural taste of the seafood without overpowering it. Every bite transported me back to a Goan kitchen where food is cooked with love and authenticity.

What sets Goa Bhavan apart is the attention to detail and consistency in taste—just like homemade Goan food, but served with finesse. The service was prompt and courteous, and the ambiance added to the overall warmth.

Whether you’re a seafood enthusiast or simply love trying traditional regional cuisine, Goa Bhavan promises a meal that’s rich, satisfying, and truly memorable. Highly recommended!❤️✨

Perfect place for fish lovers. Bombil fry, Squids Chilly, and Crab Masala are a must-try. Highly recommended 👍

featured_reviews.name: Dr Prasad Kamble
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for authentic Goan flavors in a homely setting, Goa Bhavan is the place to be! I had an amazing experience with their seafood dishes, especially the Prawns Masala, which was rich, flavorful, and perfectly spiced. The Pomfret Thali was another highlight—fresh fish cooked to perfection, served with a variety of sides that made for a wholesome and satisfying meal.

The Bombil Fry and Mandeli Fry were crispy, well-seasoned, and simply delicious, bringing out the natural taste of the seafood without overpowering it. Everything felt like it was cooked with care, just like a homemade meal.

Overall, Goa Bhavan serves delicious, homestyle Goan food that seafood lovers will truly appreciate. Highly recommended!

Thalis are sometimes unavailable (as happened during our visit), which meant ordering individual dishes and stretching the budget a bit. The variety of seafood on offer is fantastic—a true paradise for seafood lovers. Don’t miss the Solkadhi; it’s absolutely authentic. Desserts are optional and up to your preference. Enjoy your food...

featured_reviews.name: Nisikant Nayak
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Gajalee recently for seafood, and the experience was mixed. While the restaurant has a strong reputation and offers a wide variety of seafood (including crab, pomfret, oysters, and even snails), the pricing feels significantly inflated for what is essentially a standard dining setup.

For instance, crab was quoted at around ₹5000 per kg (pre-processing), and a medium-sized pomfret fry, recommended by the staff—cost about ₹2000. The taste was decent, but not proportionate to the premium pricing.

The restaurant tends to be overcrowded in the evenings, likely due to limited seafood options in the surrounding area, drawing local seafood enthusiasts. However, compared to coastal cities like Visakhapatnam, Chennai, Bhubaneswar, Kolkata, or Kochi, the prices here are almost double without a corresponding difference in quality or experience.

Overall, it may appeal to those specifically seeking seafood in this locality, but in terms of value for money, it falls short.
N.B: After having Pomfret, I have been suffering from stomach upset (Food poisoning) and currently recovering.

featured_reviews.name: Subodh Mishra
featured_reviews.review_text:
While Juhu is famous for its beach snacks and high-end cafes, the real magic happens in the kitchens that treat seafood with the respect it deserves. This isn't just a meal; it’s a deep dive into the culinary traditions of the Konkan coast.
The Ambiance
Don't expect minimalist chic. The vibe here is "busy Sunday lunch." It’s loud, efficient, and smells heavenly. The decor is usually simple because the owners know you aren't there to look at the walls—you’re there for the crab.
The Standout Dishes
Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck): A local must-have. It’s light, crisp on the outside, and melts like butter the moment it hits your tongue. If it doesn't crunch, it's not authentic.
Butter Garlic Pepper Crab: This is the messiest, most rewarding dish on the menu. The meat is succulent, and the sauce is so rich you’ll want to mop it up with a Neer Dosa.
Surmai (Kingfish) Thali: For the solo diner or the traditionalist. A thick, spicy masala fry served alongside a bowl of soul-warming Sol Kadhi (a pink, tangy coconut milk appetizer).
The Verdict
The service is brisk—they expect you to eat, enjoy, and make room for the next hungry patron. It’s a bit pricey compared to street food, but for the freshness of the catch, it’s worth every rupee.
Pro Tip: Always ask for the "Catch of the Day" before looking at the menu. If the Pomfret is fresh, don't overthink it—just order it.

The staff appeared inattentive, and one item, which is one of the signatures recommended by the staff ( king prawn) was served incorrectly / extremely cold which was disappointing. Basic service standards and attention to detail were lacking throughout the visit.

With improved staff training and better guest engagement, this restaurant has strong potential, as the food itself is commendable. I hope to see improvements in service on future visits.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Tanatan near Juhu Beach on Christmas Eve for lunch. The first thing that stands out about the place is its beautiful interiors — they are quite impressive and give off a royal, grand kind of vibe. The ambience definitely adds to the overall dining experience. They also had live music during the daytime, which created a pleasant and lively atmosphere.

The service, however, was average. The staff was polite, but the food preparation and service took longer than expected, so you might have to wait a bit for your order to arrive at the table.

In terms of food, I ordered the tandoori chicken. Unfortunately, it wasn’t the best experience. The chicken was slightly burnt on the sides and, considering the price, the portion size and quality didn’t really justify the cost. The place felt a bit on the expensive side overall.

I’m rating this place 3 stars mainly because of the ambience and the overall experience the restaurant offers. However, the food quality and pricing could definitely be improved to match the premium feel of the place.

featured_reviews.name: Avni Barai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had such a lovely dinner at Tanatan, Juhu last night with friends! The vibe was great, but the food honestly stole the show.

We started with the Avocado Thecha—a super unique twist with just the right balance of creamy and spicy. The Zucchini Paneer Roll was another standout, really fresh and flavourful.

The Firangi Nuska was interesting and well-executed, and the Tandoori Butter Roti paired perfectly with the comforting Dal Khichdi—simple, but done so well.

For drinks, Anar Ka Pyaar was refreshing and not overly sweet. And desserts were a total highlight—Killer Kit Kat was indulgent and fun, while the Rajasthani Ghevar added a nice traditional touch to end the meal.

Overall, a great mix of innovative and comforting dishes. Definitely a place I’d come back to!

featured_reviews.name: Akshay Hatiskar
featured_reviews.review_text: Had an amazing dining experience at Tanatan where the ambience instantly sets the mood with classy interiors, warm lighting, and soothing live music that makes the evening feel special and lively at the same time. We started with the Bhuna Chaap which was smoky, flavorful, and perfectly cooked with tender texture in every bite. The Murg Bharwaan Lahori was rich and indulgent with delicious stuffing and a creamy gravy that had bold authentic flavors. The Lucknowi Nihari stood out with its deep aromatic taste and slow cooked meat that was extremely soft and full of spices. The Chicken Biryani was fragrant and well layered with balanced flavors and juicy chicken pieces that made it very satisfying. Cheese Garlic Naan was soft, buttery, and generously filled with cheese, pairing beautifully with the gravies. The cocktails Penicillin and South Side were refreshing and well crafted, one offering smoky citrus notes and the other giving a light minty freshness that complemented the food perfectly. featured_reviews.name: Sandip Samani
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review with a sense of utter disbelief and disappointment. My visit to Bora Bora in Juhu was, without exaggeration, one of the most baffling restaurant experiences I have ever had.

On a Sunday evening, when one expects a restaurant to be at its busiest, the place was nearly empty. We now understand exactly why.

From the moment we were seated, it felt like we were being told "no" to everything we asked for. The series of disappointments went as follows:

1. No Indian Beer: When we asked for a popular Indian beer, we were simply told, "We don't have Indian beer." No alternative suggestions, just a dead end.
2. No Tandoori Chicken: We then tried to order a classic Indian starter, the Tandoori Chicken, only to be informed that "tandoor dishes are not available." For a restaurant that has "Indian food" on its menu, this was a major red flag.
3. The Final Blow - No Indian Food At All: As a last resort, we looked at their Indian main course selections. After deciding, we were then given the most shocking reason of all: they could not serve any Indian food because their "gas cooker was spoilt."

Let that sink in. A restaurant was unable to cook an entire cuisine from its own menu due to a broken appliance, and saw no issue with still operating and seating customers.

We left utterly appalled after having a mediocre pizza since we were starving . The complete lack of contingency planning or even a hint of apology was staggering. The empty tables on a prime Sunday evening are not a coincidence; they are a direct consequence of gross mismanagement and a clear disregard for the customer experience.

Final Verdict: Save your time and money. This establishment is clearly not equipped to deliver on its promises. I am not just disappointed; I am angry that a restaurant can operate with such incompetence. Do not recommend.

This place has become a personal favorite when it comes to seafood—I've been a regular here, and it never disappoints!

The variety they offer is fantastic, and the quality is consistently top-notch. Despite the 1+1 seating setup, the place is always crowded, which speaks volumes about how popular it is. If you're a fan of South Indian-style seafood, you're in for a treat—their preparations really stand out.

What I love most is that it's not just tasty, but also easy on the wallet. Great seafood, great flavors, and great value—what more can you ask for?

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Harish Lunch Home for a non-veg dinner, and I have to say, my experience was quite mixed. While the restaurant does have a parking facility and offers both bar and family seating sections, the food and service left much to be desired.
This place is known for its seafood and bar setup, so I had some expectations going in. We ordered a variety of dishes:
•	Manchow Soup
•	Chicken Ghee Roast
•	Butter Garlic Prawns
•	Bombil Fry
•	Chicken Crispy
•	Egg Fried Rice

Out of everything, only the soup was passable. The chicken ghee roast was underwhelming—the masala wasn’t cooked properly. Butter garlic prawns lacked flavor and freshness, and the bombil fry didn’t meet the usual seafood standard either.

The chicken crispy was the biggest disappointment. It was hard and chewy, nowhere near the crispy texture we expected—it honestly ruined the mood of the meal.

For the main course, we ordered egg fried rice, but the waiter failed to guide us properly with portion sizes, especially considering we were a big family. This led to a shortage and overall dining discomfort.

In short, service was poor, food was mostly below average, and portion sizes were not family-friendly.
I would not recommend this place for a proper family dinner. If you’re looking for quality food and attentive service, I suggest you explore other options.

featured_reviews.name: Nakul Janglay
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Fresh Catch by Francis recently after hearing a lot about it and honestly came back with mixed feelings.

We tried -

Mushroom Butter Garlic was decent, nothing wrong with it, but nothing memorable either.

Bombil Rava Fry was probably the better dish of the lot. Crispy, tasty, and enjoyable.

Bangda Ambotic Curry was good, but felt like a standard Goan curry. Not something I’d go back specifically for.

Crab Meat Spicy Masala.
It was more like a regular seafood bhurji than a standout crab dish. Now where close to justifying the exorbitant price being charged.

Pomfret Hara Bhara Tawa Fry.
The biggest letdown. The fish didn’t feel particularly fresh, the taste was quite average, and the pricing for a small medium sized portion felt just too steep. For that kind of money (or even less) you can easily get a proper wholesome seafood thali elsewhere.

Overall, the food wasn’t bad, just pretty underwhelming for the pricing and hype. Maybe Goan flavors are intentionally subtler and my palate leans more towards Konkani/Malvani seafood.

If I’m spending that kind of money on seafood in Mumbai, places like Nav Chaitanya and Gajalee still set the benchmark for me in terms of flavor, consistency and value.

featured_reviews.name: Siddharth Bose
featured_reviews.review_text:
I got to know about this place through YouTube channel Curly Tales, that discusses the favourite food of various celebrities around the country. This place was heavily recommended over the channel by Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, hence making it easier in terms of choosing the place.

It's a restaurant that serves a vast array of seafood items and some standout dishes that are worthy of being called Legendary.

The dishes I ordered during my visit were Bomblivi fish fry, Prawn Rechada and a bowl of Mixed Sea food pulao.
Add to that, 2 mugs of kingfisher beer to help in aiding the food down the stomach correctly.

The outcome, i was absolutely in wonderland after gorging on their food like there was no tomorrow.

The Prawn Rechada was simply outstanding to another level. The flavours, reminding me of the coastal beaches of India really gave an everlasting taste to hook onto.

The mixed seafood pulao was again another real dish that was crafted amazingly by their chefs. The homemade spice aromas were so imminent that it wasn't a surprise about finishing up the dish by myself.

Overall service and management deserves a 5/5. Food deserves a 5/5 as well .

Keep up the good work.

The food was good — nothing extremely standout, but overall decent. One thing we did feel though was that everything was slightly on the pricier side for what was offered. That being said, the interiors really give you that old-school Goan tavern vibe, which added a nice charm to the experience.

featured_reviews.name: george joseph
featured_reviews.review_text: What a find. A cute little restaurant with goan vibes right in bandra. You would need to plan to be there around opening time if you want to get a seat in their cozy indoor area. They close for the evening making it a little exclusive with the time restriction. The food was really good. We ordered a chicken starter along with the prawn curry rice and pork vindaloo. The prawn curry rice combo is a must try. Coming from Kerala it gave me those beach vibes. The curry is runny and just perfect with rice. It felt just like it was made at home. The pork was incredible. The pieces they had in the vindaloo consisted of fat and flesh you always die for. Not a lot of places get this right. It was a little too sweet for my usual vindaloo but nonetheless tasty. We could not get an inside sitting spot but consider yourself lucky if you do. I'm sure the experience would be worth it. One of the best places i have visited in bandra.

featured_reviews.review_text: 14 Sept Sunday - note - most of positive reviews are fake be aware - This so-called restaurant is nothing but a disgraceful dump masquerading as a place to eat , we entered at 2:30 pm in the AC section and left at 4:45 pm, not because we were gossiping but because these jokers took 25 minutes to serve each dish even after repeatedly calling them while restaurant is not in rush hour 20% capacity guest was there , stretching the ordeal into hours of torture. featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind Lunch Home,  Pali Naka,  Bandra (west)

Jai Hind is a brightest shining star of the galaxy of coastal cuisine restaurants in Mumbai.  With the few branches spread across the city,  this branch at Bandra,  Pali Naka is their first branch.  The other one is on the Linking Road, which seems to be rather spacious and well furnished.  But as a foodie, my hunt is always for a 'Value for money'  restaurants with excellent quality and quantity and this desire of mime gets fulfilled only in humble homely restaurants.  This branch at Pali Naka has been renovated recently and has only five tables in all.  I recommend to reserve a table in the evening as its a very old and famous restaurant in the area and gets filled quite soon.

The list of dishes we ordered :

1.  Patra Ni Macchi (Basa)
2. Bombil Thali
3. Chicken Sukka Thali

Let me begin with the most yummiest first. The chicken sukka was simply top quality stuff made with supreme perfection. It was creamy with great blend of masalas and literally made us lick our fingers till the end.  The chicken pieces were one of the softest and well marinated ones I ever had.  The Bombil was crispy and crunchy on the outside and soft juicy within. The soul kadi (pink broth)  was thick and made with actual coconut milk.  The texture of the chapatis were homely and rice was soft, fresh and well cooked.

Patra Ni Macchi was steamed to ultimate perfection,  which retained the original flavour of the soft melting Basa fish.  The green stuffing on it was blend of spicy and sour.

Over all,  A must visit restaurant..
Staff is helpful

featured_reviews.name: Pereira Gynel
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place has such an amazing tropical ambience. You are welcomed by soulful Goan music, and the vibe is relaxed and unhurried. The servers don’t rush you, making it a perfect spot to truly enjoy your meal.

Mr. Merwin, the manager, took great care of us, and our servers Sonia and Edwin were humble, polite, and very prompt, obliging us with every request.

The food is unlike anything you’ve tasted.. authentic Goan cuisine rooted deeply in the culture and spices of Goa. Every dish is beautifully presented, with thoughtful plating that elevates the experience without being overdone. The cutlery, plates, and glassware are aesthetically pleasing and enhance the dining experience, without robbing you of quantity. Portions are generous and satisfying.

From the big plates, we had the Traditional Pork Sorpatel with rice, Goan-style chilli chicken, and Surmai fish curry rice. The sorpatel was so authentic it made my mum emotional...it brought back memories of old friends who had cooked traditional pork dishes in her younger days. The Goan-style chilli chicken was the standout dish of the afternoon...smooth, succulent, and packed with a powerful flavour punch. The surmai fish curry rice felt like something an old granny had made, warm, comforting, and soulful.

From the small plates, we tried the Goan fried chicken with spicy mayo...six generous boneless strips, made to order, pairing perfectly with lime and the spicy mayo. The grilled squid stuffed with crab was outstanding, with the masala truly stealing the show. The prawn balchao masala stuffed forminhas crispy tarts were tangy and well-made; while not my personal favourite, they were only overshadowed by stronger dishes. The tender coconut and raw mango salad was light, tropical, refreshing, and beautifully balanced.

For drinks, we had the Coconut Boy Refresher, Kokum Spritz, and Tamarind Trails. These are not your usual cocktails... Goan spices and flavours take centre stage, and an open mind is needed to fully enjoy them.

Coconut Boy truly lives up to its promise of 'fresh' and delivers an experience that transports you straight to Goa. Highly recommended even if you’re simply looking for some relaxed downtime with exceptional food and service.

featured_reviews.name: Everything On A Plate EOAP
featured_reviews.review_text:
AMBIENCE:

Despite being located at a busy intersection, the instant you come inside, you are taken to a tranquil and unexpectedly quiet environment. Amidst the dim lights and décor paying ode to the Goan theme, what we appreciated the most was the ample open space to move around and even dance (which our daughter did multiple times throughout the night).

FOOD:
Vegetable Cheese Rissois: Though the classic Portuguese fried pastry is usually filled with meat, we tried the vegetarian version and were not disappointed. It starts with a crumbly-soft bite which leads to a minced vegetables mixed with cheese that definitely melts in your mouth.

Mapusa Market toast with Cheese & Green Chilli: Coconut boys take on the chilli cheese toast with a twist. On first look it’s just your average cheese chilli toast, but one bite into it and you hit a tangy punch which took us by surprise…. It was mango aachaar! ‘Who would’ave thunk?’ This dish did have some mixed opinions!

Choris Chilli Fry: Choriz tossed with chilli, onion, tomato teamed up with warm, fluffy poee… we absolutely left licking our fingers. Would have gone for round two but there was more to be relished on the menu.

Grilled Squid Stuffed with Crab: A host suggestion that we absolutely jumped at the mention of! Crab meat tossed in Recheado, stuffed into a squid & grilled… a lot of effort goes into this. Hints of spice married with the sweetness of the crab meat and the bite of squid… a messy meal you must try at least once! Definitely big brownie points for the squid NOT being chewy.

Mushroom & vegetables slow cooked with Xacuti masala: A medley of steamed veggies (Mushroom, carrot, potato, cauliflower) tossed in a Xacuti gravy. You have an option of Poee or steamed rice to accompany it and we went with the latter. We requested them to hold back the spice a bit for our toddler & it’s wholesome, earthy, slightly-sweet coconut-ty broth was welcomed with a smack of the lips.

Serradura: This simple pudding can go awry in so many ways… And believe me, we've tasted some absolute disasters. But coconut boy absolutely nailed-it! The crumbly, biscuit dust alternated with fluffy, light whipped cream was what we devoured at the end of a great meal. Not too sweet, not too dense… just perfect.

Service: The service undoubtedly elevated our entire experience! We had Siddhesh giving us amazing recommendations and making sure we had everything we needed. Akbar stopped by with some fantastic banter, and last but not least, Faustin, whom our daughter adored and sat with virtually the entire dinner, allowing us to savour every bite!

SUMMING UP: If you love Goan food, it’s definitely an experience you do not want to miss. Right from the décor to the service, it’s comfy, cozy and warm. The cost is a bit on the higher end but the quality and flavors are worth every penny.

The place is very well designed keeping many things in mind. The seating is very comfortable and spacious unlike we often experience at buffet place. The price of 1600 INR for the weekday dinner gets you a full fledged meal from soups, chaat counter, salad bar, live pasta and delicacies from North India, mughlai and Asia.

Non-veg Starters had chicken cajun which had tender chicken well greased and tossed to crisp and tawa fry basa which is barely found anywhere coz basa is soft and people find it real hard to tawa fry such soft fish but here at Jeon, It wasn't just tawa fried but was fried to perfection with right marination making it all the more Delicious.

Thanks to Shadab, who was taking care of our table. He was attentive and helped us with spot-on recommendations.
.
Here's everything we tried (Highly Recommend):
1. Sumac De-light: A beautifully balanced cocktail with half vodka and half gin. It was refreshing and presented beautifully in a glass dome with smoke
2. Rehan: A light and incredibly refreshing mocktail
3. Harissa Chicken Kebab: Chicken was grilled to absolute perfection and served with a unique cream cheese dip
4. Chicken Afrikaan: A signature Pide (Turkish flatbread) dish. It was flavourful and super comforting with just the right amount of spices and chicken chunks
5. Lavash Crust Chicken Kabsa: Soo loved this! It's an aromatic spiced rice dish paired with tender chicken and a crisp lavash layer that added great texture to the dish

.
Overall, the food stood out for its depth of flavour with Middle Eastern & Mediterranean influences coming through beautifully in every dish. Everything was well-balanced, well-presented and soo delicious. A special mention for the restaurant manager, Mr. Gautam, whose warm and gracious hospitality added a personal touch to our dining experience 😊
.
Bayroute delivers on every front, be it ambience, food, drinks and service. It's worth a visit!

featured_reviews.name: Ameen Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
The ambience here is truly great and has always been a highlight 🌟. I’ve been visiting this restaurant 2-3 times a year for the last 5-7 years, and earlier, the taste they delivered was gold. Back then, they really tried to include everything in their buffet, and the dessert section used to be huge and impressive 🍰🍮.

Now, let’s talk about the breakfast buffet—it’s pretty standard, similar to what you’d find at any 5-star continental breakfast 🍳🥐. They do include a few Indian dishes, but honestly, breakfast here has never excited me since the beginning.

As for dinner, it used to be something I truly looked forward to because of how flavourful and varied the food was 🍽️. However, over the last 2-3 visits, it feels like something is always off—sometimes it’s the salt, sometimes it’s the flavours. The food feels same-same now, and perhaps I’ve become fed up of eating the same dishes repeatedly. There’s nothing new or exciting anymore, and the taste is not extraordinary enough to crave anything specific. I used to love the pizza here; it was one of my favorites. But lately, the taste has literally deteriorated 😞. It’s just not the same anymore, and it’s disappointing to see the quality drop. Hope they bring back the original flavors they were known for.

That said, this place still shines for its ambience ✨, and for newcomers, it might still feel impressive and worth the visit. But for me, my interest in visiting Lotus Cafe is slowly fading away 😕. I guess it’s a matter of having it too many times.

Still, for the overall experience, I’d rate it 4 stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐.

featured_reviews.name: Paurnima Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Coast & Bloom at Dadar and it turned out to be a truly memorable dining experience that beautifully celebrates coastal and regional Indian flavors with a refined touch.

We began with the Lobster Thermidor, which was served in a rich, creamy mushroom sauce accompanied by sautéed vegetables, bread, and a perfectly cooked egg. The dish was indulgent, flavorful, and luxuriously satisfying. Alongside, we had the Tandoori Prawns, which carried an excellent smoky char from the tandoor. Paired with fresh green chutney and a sweet-tangy mango pickle, the combination elevated the entire starter experience.

For the main course, we opted for the Malvani Fish Curry with Ravas. The fish was exceptionally fresh, tender, and cooked to perfection, soaking beautifully in the aromatic Malvani gravy. We also tried the Chettinad Chicken, which had a bold, spicy profile and was packed with deep, authentic flavors.

To complement the curries, we had Malabar Parotta, Ghavane, and Chilli Cheese Garlic Naan. Each bread brought a different texture and paired wonderfully with the gravies, with the ghavane being a particularly delightful and unique accompaniment.

We also enjoyed Solkadi, which perfectly balanced the meal with its refreshing, lightly spiced tanginess. For drinks, we tried the Ratamba (kokum-based), Navy Punch, and Ginger Ale, all of which were refreshing and well-crafted.

To end the meal, we had the Crab Meat Fried Rice. While pleasant, this was comparatively simpler in flavor and had lesser crab meat than expected.

What truly stood out, beyond the food, was the exceptional service. The staff member assisting us went above and beyond — offering curry samples when we were confused between options and even showing us the raw fish to help us understand the portion and quality we would be served. Such thoughtful hospitality added immense value to the experience.

The entire meal came to ₹8,236, and considering the quality of ingredients, variety of dishes, and outstanding service, it felt well worth the price.

Coast & Bloom is a must-visit for anyone who appreciates coastal cuisine served with elegance, authenticity, and warm hospitality.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This is an iconic restaurant of Bombay and already a legend. You can see photos of celebrities on walls who have visited the place.
This is fine dine place and might feel expensive but the experience you get here will last for long time. It has set a high benchmark in terms of ambience, service and food.

featured_reviews.name: Selvamanojkumar S
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goa Portuguese Restrobar at Mahim is a restaurant filled with history and aromas. The owners of the restaurant is very thoughtful in creating the ambience, delightful handpicked menu and the soulful light music completes the experience.

They have bought the authentic Goan, local Maharastrian and selected specials from various parts of South India all at one plate. And one cannot believe it, they have done justice to each one of it. Their fusion dishes are must try, felt oil can be reduced a bit. Highly recommended place for a quality time spent and for all food lovers.

featured_reviews.name: Nive Raitz von Frentz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Thirty six years this place has been around, it was my first time.

There are three types of cuisines (Goan, south Indian and Maharashtrian), so the menu is extensive (too much choice?), but attractive photos of certain signature dishes help narrow down the choice!

In the end I opted for choriz pulao with a side of crispy bhindi.

Even for the super hungry, the portions are huge, perhaps with a view to sharing.

Towards the end of our lunch, it got a bit loud from larger, neighbouring tables.

The good news is that you are presented with a discount coupon to use for next time.

featured_reviews.name: Kaivan Doctor
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the oldest & best restaurants serving Goan food in Mumbai.
Excellent ambience & service.
Live guitarist on weekends.
Wide variety of vegetarian  & non-vegetarian dishes.
Special mention stuffed crab,chicken Bali Bali,neer dosa & Prawn gassi with rice.
Worth visiting multiple times though rates are slightly on higher side.

featured_reviews.name: travofood
featured_reviews.review_text: I loved the stuffed bombil with prawn. The ambience is awesome. Somehow the chicken pulao was just ok and the chicken pieces were a bit hard. Well, this the usual issue in Mumbai for the most of the chicken thing.parking is available as valet. This is definitely one big advantage in this part of the city. Courteous staff to attend you all the time. Good vibes with in house singer with a guitar to play your favourite requests.

featured_reviews.name: Hrishikesh Chinchalikar
featured_reviews.review_text:
🌴 A Heartwarming Goan Experience at a Portuguese Restaurant 🌴

Dining at this Goan Portuguese restaurant was truly a delightful experience. From the first bite to the last note of live music, everything felt authentic, soulful, and unforgettable.

The food was absolutely amazing—rich in flavor, perfectly balanced, and deeply rooted in Goan tradition. Every dish reflected care, passion, and mastery of recipes passed down through generations.

⭐ Special Dishes We Tried:

Coconut Cashew Bhaji – A standout vegetarian dish, creamy, mildly spiced, and incredibly comforting. The coconut and cashew combination was simply delicious.

Surmai Fish Kalvam – A must-try for fish lovers. Fresh surmai cooked in a flavorful Goan-style curry that was bold, aromatic, and unforgettable.

Live Music by Uncle – The soulful live music added magic to the evening, creating a warm and joyful Goan vibe that elevated the entire dining experience.

What truly made this place special was the personal touch. The owner personally visited every table, warmly sharing the inspiring journey of how the restaurant began. He spoke about his wife’s culinary journey and her exceptional talent as a cook—the heart behind the delicious recipes served here. Listening to their story made the food taste even better, knowing it comes from passion, dedication, and love.

The restaurant has grown into multiple branches, including international locations, and it’s easy to see why. This place is not just about food—it’s about culture, stories, and genuine hospitality.

✨ Highly recommended for anyone who loves authentic Goan cuisine, soulful music, and heartfelt hospitality. A place you’ll want to visit again and again.

featured_reviews.name: Leena Surve
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goa Portuguese is a must stop in my every visit to Mumbai (from USA). This place has such a fun vibe with awesome food. There Goan and malvani dishes remind me of my mom’s home cooking.   We always start with Bombay duck fry and shrimp koliwada. Then the order including tisarya sukhe, chicken xacuti, pomfret / surmai dishes, amboli, vade continues so much that we get warned by the waiter ‘jara jast hoil ho’ (might be little to much). But we love their food so much that the warning, even though correct, gets ignored.
Even after visiting so many times, we have managed to touch very less amounts of dishes offered. Must increase our visits.
This time was lucky to meet with Dr. Suhas Awchat (co-founder). A warm personality and all the praise for master chef, Mrs. Deepa Awchat (he openly gave the credit of starting and owning the restaurant completely  to her, indicating that after army, she is his boss 😀).
Awesome food, fun atmosphere, good - helpful staff. Definitely a must visit place.

featured_reviews.name: Ameya Bellare
featured_reviews.review_text: Been to this place after 15 yrs... It still retains the charm. The place and the food continues to be the highlight. What I love most is the ability to order all western cuisines (Maharashtrian, Konkan, Goan and Deccan). The only difficulty is to order them all. Strongly recommend going in a group so you can try the variety offered at this place. All this while witnessing humble bragging at its best!

featured_reviews.name: sonia mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
It’s been a while since we’ve enjoyed an authentic Maharashtrian meal! At first glance the place makes your feel right at home, very true to its name! We had such a great meal on Sunday, we were three of us - my brother, my sister and I.
The best thing to do when you visit is let the owner suggest their specials for you to eat, we didn’t even open the menu - we tried the Chonak Fry - 10/10, we tried the Bombil fry- 12/10 ( the filling inside the Bombil blew our mind, we had the Alu Wadi with Prawns filling - 10/10!
For main course we had the Amti with Rice Bhakri and Ravas Fry ( the Ravas so incredibly fresh) the main course was 10/10 and to top it off we also tried their Prawns Bhaat / Pulav - it was so damn good! 100/10….the Sol Kadis we tasted took us back home honestly. After this meal all we needed was our bed to sleep on cause we were in a complete food coma. An absolutely outstanding meal with a very comfortable seating and ambiance! A definite must visit again and again!

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Fish Curry Rice is a true celebration of coastal flavours and seafood mastery. Their seafood spread is outstanding — the surmai and pomfret are impeccably fresh, the halwa and bombil melt beautifully, and the fish fry along with the prawns curry are rich, fragrant, and deeply satisfying.

What truly stole the show were the tisrya sukka, mori masala, and kalva sukka — bold, soulful preparations that burst with authentic coastal character. The must-try list is long for a reason: prawns aluwadi, stuffed pomfret, bombil thecha fry, and chounak fry are each crafted with precision and irresistible flavour.

Their thalis deserve special praise — generous, well-balanced, and layered with flavour, offering a complete journey through coastal cuisine. A special mention to owner Sandesh Bhat — the heart and soul of FCR — who ensures taste and consistency are always bang on, and who, along with his attentive team, is always on his toes with spot-on recommendations tailored to your mood and palate.

A place where freshness meets finesse, and every plate tells a story of spice, sea, and tradition.

featured_reviews.name: KPExplorer
featured_reviews.review_text: This resturant in primiraly from Pune which is only one in Mumbai Dadar kohinoor is was way beyond expectations .. good try for fish lovers, with great service from staff to decently priced thalis. They start with timbal a kokum drink as apetiser. Their fish curry is very delicious with perfect taste. They also serve senior citizen thali at 450 in which they gave 2 fish fry. Crab thali was also great. Their Ghavna with curry is an amazing combination

featured_reviews.name: guptepooja
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent place and way better than the Pune branch. It's open from 11.30am to 11pm...so you get served even at 5pm

They cook fresh stuff so order may take time but it's fresh! Amazing taste and super fresh fish. Blessed to have this joint in Dadar which works as a perfect combination of fresh seafood+ authentic goan cuisine+ economical.  We ordered mutton + pomfret fry thali and chicken thali. Fish was super duper fresh. My 6yrs old child finished the meals with no left over food in her plate; which itself is a big compliment.

Soham manages this really well. He also gifted a small soft toy fish to my child for new years.

Let the photos do the justice.

featured_reviews.name: Floyd Pinto
featured_reviews.review_text:
Been on the lookout for good fish thalis in and around dadar

FCR is a very nice place to have one

Reasonable price, well prepared and the quantity served is also not bad

Wide range of thalis from mini to special to varying types

Spacious seating and quick service too

featured_reviews.name: Sunit Katkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Saw a lot of food vloggers show this place. Big mistake of believing them. Only good thing is the welcome drink called Tival. The prawns sukka was more curry and rubber like prawns. Only slightly better dish was crab masala. Sol kadhi had no kick. Maybe Gajalee and Sindhudurg have spoilt me by giving very good Sol Kadhi. We asked for Rice Bhakri expecting it to be soft like other places. This felt like it was cooked a day before and just reheated and served. It was too hard to be called a rice Bhakri.

Regret not going to Dutta Boarding House in Parel or even Gomantak next door. Had crab masala last week at Dutta Boarding.. FCR does not have that zing but it's better than the rubber prawn sukka taste.

Sorry, will not believe food vloggers from now on.

featured_reviews.name: Harshad Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text: Small and cozy. Delicious food. Service is excellent. Prawns Aluwadi is a must try dish.

featured_reviews.name: Manish Bhogade

But as a veg eater, I honestly didn’t enjoy the veg thali at all. If you’re vegetarian, don’t go in with high expectations. For non-veg folks, it’s absolutely worth it.”

featured_reviews.name: Ayush G
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Seafood Disaster – Masooli Restaurant

Visited Masooli expecting good seafood. What we got was very disappointing.

We ordered crab garlic, surmai garlic masala, bombil thecha fry, surmai green masala, rice with plain fish curry, solkadi and lime soda. The only real savior in the entire meal was the surmai green masala. The solkadi and lime soda were fine.

Everything else was a letdown. The fish curry had no tanginess, no salt, no flavour. It tasted flat and unfinished. For a seafood restaurant, getting a basic fish curry wrong is shocking. The crab garlic and bombil thecha fry were also disappointing.

I even called the waiter and asked him to taste the fish curry himself. He did not argue or defend it. He was so sure I was right that he did not even attempt to try it.

Service was good and the waiter was polite and attentive. But good service cannot save bad food.

Prices are high, but the taste does not justify it at all. Very disappointing experience. Would not return.

featured_reviews.name: Sandeep Kanchan
featured_reviews.review_text: Green masala Pomfret was fresh and good, prawns thali was okay, caramel custard was nice. Overall Ambience okay, food quality decent not outstanding for the price.

featured_reviews.name: Nameeta Chikhalkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Masoli recently and honestly, the experience was very disappointing. The service was pathetic — no staff attended to us until we had to repeatedly ask, even for basic things like water. Drinks were served late, and overall, there was no attentiveness at all.

The food was another letdown. We ordered Pomfret Fry which was undercooked, with most of the flesh still raw. The Bombil Thali was completely bland — the javla had no taste and no salt (even after adding salt, it was flavorless). The kolambi masala was extremely spicy but without any real taste or balance, and I usually have a high spice tolerance. On top of that, the bhakri served was not rice bhakri but maida, chewy and totally off.

Special mention to the staff handling our table, Manish — he was not attentive at all and definitely needs to be trained in customer service. If customers are paying their hard-earned money, the least expected is basic hospitality and properly cooked food.

Overall, a very poor experience.
Not at all worthy to visit there are many more place which u people can try it worthless

featured_reviews.name: Padam Bhushan
featured_reviews.review_text: I went to this eatery on a friend's recommendation. It's a modest space with cosily placed tables. The ambiance and maintenance are typical of a mid-range restaurant. The food is really fresh and tasty, though I had to limit myself to a few options because the most of food items are from Konkani cuisine, which is very hot and spicy. Whatever I ate was delicious, and they deserve full marks for it. However, the prices of each item are rather high, making my total experience less enjoyable. I would recommend this restaurant, but only if you are willing to pay exorbitant rates!

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Thakur
featured_reviews.review_text: After long time, we enjoyd delicious non veg food. Maasoli is situated in Dadar West opp. Veena world office. customer_updates.text:
The restaurant serves authentic Maharashtrian cuisine, and it was an outstanding experience. We started with Agri Matka and Chulivarcha Chicken, both of which were bursting with flavor. The Agri Matka had that traditional rustic touch, slow-cooked to perfection, while the Chulivarcha Chicken, prepared on a traditional clay stove, was smoky, tender, and incredibly delicious.

For starters, we tried the Prawn Sukka, which was a perfect blend of spices, with succulent prawns cooked in a dry, aromatic masala. It was the ideal start to the meal. We also couldn't resist the Prawn Biryani, which was fragrant and loaded with juicy prawns. The balance of spices and flavors in every dish was just spot on.
Overall, this restaurant is a must-visit for anyone craving authentic Maharashtrian food. Every dish was prepared with care, and the flavors stayed true to the region's culinary heritage. I can't wait to go back and try more!

customer_updates.name: Tushar Chalke
customer_updates.text: If you like Fish and gavran chicken food then this is the place you should visit. The price is quite reasonable, the food is excellent ,the quantity is filling,the service is fantastic. It is value for money MUST TRY Chulivarcha Chicken.

featured_reviews.name: honest reviewer

Had ordered Kokum soda, caramel custard, prawns thali and squid fry.
Kokum soda was a refreshing but to concentrated, caramel custard was my personal favourite, prawns thali was amazing however they could have levelled up the spices slightly in the gravy and dry prawns bhaji, Solkadhi was best and squid fry were just slightly bland should have ordered chilli squid fry. The flavours were slightly on the spicier side but quite flavourful.

featured_reviews.name: Saket Shrirao
featured_reviews.review_text: Ordered one pomfret thali . Fish was fresh and very good. But the fish curry had only curry and not fish . Normally they give one piece of small fish too. featured_reviews.name: Neel Shrivatra
featured_reviews.review_text: Best thing was, as we entered they welcomed us and inside it was no smell like other seafood restaurants. Service very good. Food tastes very authentic and feels good. Ramesh Nakte, served us very well throughout our food experience suggesting all new and famous food they have.

featured_reviews.name: Manjiri Chalke
featured_reviews.review_text: Had an amazing experience at Nav Mejwani & Seafood Restaurant! The seafood was super fresh, flavorful, and cooked perfectly. From the authentic coastal taste to the warm hospitality, everything was just perfect. A great place to enjoy delicious seafood with family and friends. Definitely worth visiting again!

featured_reviews.name: H Nanda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located in Dadar, on the busy gokhale road, this non veg restaurant is known for sea food.  Restaurant is clean and well maintained.   Service is also clean and neat.  While sea food is good, chicken items are quite ordinary ( tried chicken biryani, butter chicken - nothing great).  On the other hand prawn dishes were good.  Food preparation is Maharashtrian flavor.   Prices are reasonable.
Peak times and peak days would have some wait time to get the table.  Parking is a major problem,  though they have valet service board, I do know where are going to park your vehicle.   Nearest known parking is near Shivaji Park or Kohinoor mall ( BMC  Parking), both about a kilometer away.  I have had food here about five to six times.  Worth a try.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A delightful meal at Flavors of Malvan in Prabhadevi! The food is exceptionally tasty, wholesome, and prepared in a way that feels truly home-style, yet packed with authentic coastal flavors.

The Green Chutney Surmai was outstanding, the Fish Curry with rice was comforting and flavorful, and the Koliwada Prawns were perfectly cooked and absolutely delicious. To top it all, the Kokum Soda was simply mind-blowing—refreshing, tangy, and the perfect accompaniment to the meal.

A special mention to Vinod and Navin, who were incredibly warm, welcoming, and attentive. They took the time to understand our preferences and suggested dishes that suited our tastes perfectly, making the dining experience even more enjoyable.

If you're looking for authentic Malvani cuisine that combines traditional flavors with heartfelt hospitality, this place is a must-visit!The restaurant is Flavors of Malvan.

featured_reviews.name: Sankar Kasirajan
featured_reviews.review_text:
It was my daughter's birthday eve, and after some gentle persuasion to choose Pallavi's boutique café over Mumbai stalwarts like Trishna or Mahesh, we were seated in this beautifully done-up spot near Dadar's Shivaji Park. Though small, the space possesses a premium, fine-dining ambiance.

The Feast
Despite claiming to be "light eaters" (ahem!), we indulged in a vast selection, and every single dish was amazing. The true "Flavours" of Malwan shone through, outperforming many other seafood restaurants I've visited over the past 28 years (including Gajalee, Mahesh Lunch Home, and Sindhudurg).
Our order included:
	Refreshing Drinks: Sol Kadi, Kokum Soda, and Lemon Soda.
	Signature Seafood: Chutney Stuffed Pomfret Fry with Prawns, Chutney Stuffed Bombil Roll with Prawns, Sukka Crab, Tisrya Sukka, and Prawn Curry, paired with Rice Bhakri.
	Desserts: Ukdiche Modak and Puran Poli.

The Unforgettable Star
While every item was a feast for the taste buds, the Sukka Crab was the undisputed champion—absolutely outstanding! We literally wiped the plates clean and even drank the leftover Prawn Curry. This is food made with passion; food that truly leaves a lasting memory.

My words and photos simply cannot do full justice to the culinary magic at "Flavours of Malwan."

Don't just read about it—experience the authentic, soulful taste of Malwani cuisine for yourself!

featured_reviews.name: Anvi Kaale
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently had lunch at this restaurant and it was truly a fantastic experience! Authentic malvani taste.😋 The flavors were absolutely amazing, and every dish was prepared to perfection. 💯 I highly recommend trying their delicious offerings. Will definitely be back for more! ✨👍

featured_reviews.name: Preeti Parab
featured_reviews.review_text:
The ambience of the restaurant was lovely and cozy. We tried the Bombil Tawa Fry, but it was quite oily. We also ordered the Surmai Thali and Pomfret Thali. Everything in the thali was good except for the fish curry, which unfortunately lacked flavor. Solkadi was fresh and awesome in taste.

For desserts, we tried Modak and Puranpoli. The Modak tasted good, although the outer covering was a bit thick.The Puranpoli, however, was absolutely awesome and definitely a highlight.

Overall, it’s a nice and cozy restaurant, especially for non-vegetarian lovers. 🐟🍽️

featured_reviews.name: Nitin Guddeti
featured_reviews.review_text: Had a wonderful experience at Flavours of Malvan! The Prawns pulav and Bombil Thali were absolutely delicious, packed with authentic Malvani flavors. Fresh seafood, flavorful curries, crispy fry, and refreshing solkadhi made the meal truly satisfying. Highly recommended for seafood lovers looking for an authentic taste of the coast. 🐟🦐😋

featured_reviews.name: Greeshma Gowda
featured_reviews.review_text: Walked into this restaurant when we were in Dadar on a Sunday evening. Its a small restaurant on the ground floor of a residential buidling. There was a waiting time of 30 mins to get in. We ordered the pomfret thalli and crab thalli. The service is slow but it was worth the wait. The crab was soft and well cooked and the gravy was delicious. We also had sweet lime soda and lemon ginger drink. Last we had ukdiche modak which was also tasty.

featured_reviews.name: Meghna Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Everything tasted like it was cooked in someone’s very talented Malvani aaji’s kitchen. The bombil fry? Illegal levels of good. The mutton sukka + the prawn thali? Had me contemplating licking the plate. The puran poli and the modaks? Felt like a hug in dessert form. Just solid recommendations from the team and great vibes all around.
If you like your food flavourful, fiery, and with zero nonsense, this place is a no-brainer. Will 100% be back.

featured_reviews.name: Jimeet Pawaskar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Found my new favorite Sunday spot! Being a Malvani…this place is lovely, understated home-style charm that makes you want to settle in and stay a while.
Even with a 45-minute wait on a Sunday, the staff remained gracious and efficient. The Mutton Special Thali is a must-try—rich, authentic, and perfectly executed. It felt less like eating at a restaurant and more like a high-end home-cooked feast!

featured_reviews.name: Ilina Banerjee
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tandel's Kitchen in Mahim Seafood Plaza is an extraordinary culinary gem where the ladies of the Koli community masterfully prepare some of the best seafood I've ever tasted. Nestled along the scenic Mahim Sea Beach, with a breathtaking view of the Bandra-Worli Sealink and the soothing Arabian Sea breeze, this place offers more than just food—it's an experience.

During my visit, I had the pleasure of trying several dishes, each leaving a lasting impression. The Surmai Fry was nothing short of spectacular. The fish was incredibly fresh, a testament to their daily fishing activities, and it was cooked to perfection with a flavorful blend of spices that brought out the best in the surmai.

The Prawn Fry was another highlight. The prawns had a perfectly crispy outer layer that gave way to tender, juicy insides. The balance of textures and the well-seasoned coating made each bite a delight.

One of the most memorable dishes was the Clams Masala Curry. It was delightfully spicy, striking a perfect balance that kept it exciting without being overwhelming. The curry had a chatpata (tangy and spicy) taste that was utterly addictive. Paired with the extremely soft Bhakri (a type of flatbread), it created a harmonious combination that was both comforting and satisfying.

What sets Tandel's Kitchen apart is not only the freshness of their seafood but also the unique spice mixes they create in-house. These spices, prepared in a homely style, infuse the dishes with flavors that are rich, vibrant, and authentically Koli.

The ambiance of Tandel's Kitchen significantly enhances the dining experience. Enjoying such flavorful seafood while overlooking the serene Arabian Sea and the iconic Bandra-Worli Sealink, all with the cool sea breeze enveloping you, creates a dining atmosphere that is both relaxing and invigorating.

Tandel's Kitchen is a must-visit for anyone seeking an authentic and extraordinary seafood experience in Mumbai. The combination of fresh, expertly cooked seafood, unique and flavorful spices, and a perfect seaside setting makes it a standout destination. Whether you are a local or a visitor, this place promises a meal that you will not forget.

featured_reviews.name: durgesh gawde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind is a gem for seafood lovers, offering an impressive variety of dishes, generous portions, and prices that feel genuinely value-for-money. If you’re someone who appreciates fresh, well-cooked fish without burning a hole in your pocket, this restaurant easily stands out as one of the best options in the city.

One of the first things you notice at Jai Hind is the sheer range on the menu. From classics like Surmai Fry, Bombil Fry, Rawas Curry, and Prawns Koliwada to specials like Crab Masala and Tawa Pomfret, the restaurant ensures there’s something for every seafood enthusiast. What makes the experience even better is that the quality is consistent. The fish is fresh, perfectly marinated, and cooked with authentic coastal flavours that highlight Mumbai’s rich culinary heritage.

Quantity is another major plus. Unlike many seafood places where portions feel small for the price, Jai Hind gives you hearty servings that truly justify every rupee. Whether you order a thali or an à la carte dish, the plates come generously loaded, making it easy to share or enjoy as a filling meal on your own. Their fish thalis, in particular, are a standout—they offer a balanced combination of fried fish, curry, rice, chapati, and sides, making it both wholesome and satisfying.

The pricing is surprisingly reasonable, especially considering the rising cost of seafood in the city. For the quality and quantity provided, the restaurant manages to keep its rates fair, which is a big reason people return. It’s a great place for regular seafood cravings without feeling guilty about overspending.

The ambience is simple, clean, and comfortable—nothing overly fancy, but perfectly suited for a relaxed and enjoyable meal. Service is prompt, friendly, and attentive, with staff who are happy to recommend dishes based on your taste preferences.

featured_reviews.name: vaibhav palande
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Gomuntak Restaurant and tried a variety of their thalis — chicken thali, surmai thali, prawns thali, and bangda thali.

The service was quick, which is a plus. The food was decent overall, but the spice level was quite mild. When it comes to fish dishes, a slightly higher spice level is usually expected, so that was a bit disappointing. The fish quality was okay, nothing exceptional.

On the brighter side, I personally liked their wade and the gravy, which stood out more than the main dishes. We also tried prawns lollipop, which was okay.

Overall, a decent place with fast service, but could be better if the flavors were a bit more bold.

featured_reviews.name: Abhishek Bakshe
featured_reviews.review_text:
The food here is definitely the highlight—authentic Goan and Konkani cuisine that’s full of flavor and absolutely worth trying. A solid 5/5 for taste. The service is also quite good, with quick and attentive staff who manage things efficiently.

However, the overall experience is slightly affected by the atmosphere. The waiting time can be quite long, and the seating feels a bit too cramped, especially if you’re visiting with a larger group. It’s cozy, but not very comfortable in that sense.

Overall, great food and good service, but be prepared for a wait and limited space.

featured_reviews.name: Kalpana Bhandare
featured_reviews.review_text:
recently visited Gumantak Restaurant, Dadar, but unfortunately my experience was not good.
The food quality was disappointing. The rice bhakari was very bad and hard, and even the plain rice was not properly cooked. The fish gravy was tasteless and lacked proper seasoning.
Honestly, even a roadside ₹100 thali tasted much better than this meal.
I hope the restaurant takes this feedback seriously and improves their food quality

featured_reviews.name: Francis Britto
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dadar Gomantak is famous for simple, authentic Maharashtrian coastal food, especially dishes from the Konkan and Malvan regions. People love it because the food tastes homemade, spicy, fresh, and full of traditional flavors.

Great Indian restaurant right across from the Sea Princess Hotel! The food was absolutely delicious and very reasonably priced. The butter chicken was amazing, and honestly everything we ordered was excellent. Portions are generous too, so you definitely get good value.
One thing to note — even the “mild” spice level can be quite spicy since the food is authentically prepared. If you just politely brush it off, it’s no big deal.
Overall, highly recommend this spot if you’re craving authentic Indian food near the hotel!

featured_reviews.review_text: Fresh fish and good vibes all around. The ravas tandoori and bombil fry were topsssss, fresh, flavorful, and done just right. Loved it so much, I had to go in for a second round of the ravas. And the uncle serving us? Warm, calm, and genuinely kind, made the whole experience even better..

featured_reviews.name: R. Doug Wicker
featured_reviews.review_text: Wonderful, charming establishment. We were looking for a place to eat near our hotel and New Grand Family Restaurant had a high Google rating so we gave it a go. We had peri peri fries and vegetable spring rolls to start, followed by tandoori tika chicken and Singapore fried noodles with chicken. Way too much to eat for the two of us, so the noodles fell to the wayside as we rapidly filled up. Our waiter was an incredibly friendly and helpful chap from Nepal who helped us in our selections, including a delightful ice dessert that tasted of pistachio. Including a 650ml beer and Scheppes lime, our bill came to under $21 USD. You simply cannot go wrong with this place.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely loved my experience at Kerala Kitchen & Bar by Tanatan ❤️
The ambience is so beautiful and calming, gives proper luxury/fine dining vibes. The interiors, lighting and overall setup are honestly stunning. Food was amazing, especially the flavours and presentation, and even the drinks were really good.

Service was also top notch, staff was very polite and attentive throughout. Plus they have valet parking which made it super convenient.

Overall had a really nice time here with great food, ambience and service. Definitely a place I’d visit again ✨⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

featured_reviews.name: melanie pais
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kerala Kitchen & Bar is hands down one of the most delightful dining experiences I’ve had in a long time.

From the very first sip to the last bite, everything was exceptional—the drinks were refreshing, the milkshakes indulgent, and every course that followed just kept getting better. The starters were packed with authentic flavours, the main course was rich and comforting, and the desserts were the perfect sweet ending. Truly, some of the best Kerala cuisine I’ve ever tasted.
What makes this place even more special is the ambience—it genuinely transports you to Kerala. Serene, beautiful, and thoughtfully designed, it creates a calming escape right in the middle of Juhu.
The staff deserves a special mention—warm, attentive, and incredibly kind, they make you feel right at home. It’s also wonderfully kid-friendly, making it perfect for family outings.
This is not just a one-time visit kind of place—I’ll definitely be coming back with family and friends. If you love great food, great vibes, and heartfelt hospitality, this one is an absolute must-visit.

featured_reviews.name: Umesh Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Great place, the moment you enter this Resturant you get a different and pleasant feel. We being vegetarian, ordered all veg food, started with Rasam Soup followed by Neer Dosa, Set Dosa, Persactu Dosa,Thate Idli and
papaya-Paysam. Every items were tasty we enjoyed thoroughly. The service was very quick, the entire team serving all the tables were excellent , the place is very clean. Best part is the food is very light and has good after taste as well.
We advise them to have veg and non-veg sitting arrangement separate so vegetarians are comfortable. The first half from entrance gate should be offered to vegetarian/Veg section and one after that should be non veg section.
Over all it’s an excellent place and would love to visit this place again

featured_reviews.name: Anish Karkera
featured_reviews.review_text:
New place in juhu we decided to visit on a whim. The chemmeen cheriya ulli perattu is a perfect starter that's goes with parotta, only problem is that the parotta was not good. Very flat barely any fluff or flakes in it.
The kanava crispy fry was a let down, it's just fried squid with no flavour.  They didn't give us any dips or chutney with it.
Chemmeen manga curry was the hero of the afternoon. Tasty, tangy, full of prawns and raw mango. What's not to like. We paired them with freshly made appams and neer dosa.
The seafood biryani wasn't bad either, good flavour and full of prawns and squid.

The service was decent but it was disappointing to see that they served every table with fryuns and chutney but not us.  It's a small thing but it still is weird.
Still, I'm definitely going back again to try some of their other items.

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place with my ex-colleagues, and to be honest, The vibe of the place is great for spending time with family.

We ordered quite a few dishes including prawns masala fry, bombil masala, bombil rawa fry, grilled pomfret, crab lollipop, chicken, and finally prawns biryani.

Talking about the food, the crab lollipop was interesting. It obviously felt like frozen food, but the taste was still good. However, most of the seafood dishes were a little disappointing for us. The fish dishes were not spicy enough and lacked that strong flavor we were expecting. The stuffed pomfret was just okay-okay and felt more like boiled fish rather than properly fried.

We also ordered a chicken dish and specifically requested it to be spicy, but unfortunately, it turned out a bit sweet, and none of us really liked it.

But the highlight of the meal was definitely the prawns biryani. It was really, really good and honestly the best dish we had there.

Overall, the ambience and company made the experience enjoyable, but food-wise, only a few dishes really stood out for us.

featured_reviews.name: hemali kantharia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our go-to family dinner spot for any and every occasion. From small celebrations to casual dinners, this place has always been our first choice. Over time we’ve tried almost everything on the menu, and every visit somehow turns into another food memory with family.

If there are two dishes I would recommend to anyone visiting, it has to be the Bombil Fry and Peri Peri Bombil. They are easily my brother’s and my absolute favourites perfectly crispy, full of flavour, and something we end up ordering almost every single time.

And no meal here feels complete without the Kokum Sarbat or Kokum Soda. That refreshing, tangy punch of flavour just balances the seafood so well and makes the whole experience even better.

Good food, great flavours, and the comfort of family dinners this place truly feels special to us. Easily one of the best seafood restaurants and definitely a spot we’ll keep coming back to.

featured_reviews.name: Mitesh Parmar
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was the final restaurant I attended on my trip and a great place to end on.

Unfortunately at the time of our attendance the A/C was not in working order which the manager/owner advised on prior to entering, however we still went in as they had fans going on.

Didn't plan to eat a lot but to take in the delights on offer as again this was a place recommended.

We were given good information by the manager on some of the dishes and on ordering the food arrived after a short time. temperatures were on point and flavours were amazing. The prawn starters were so good, especially the Prawns Garlic Butter, so much so we ordered another tray. I also order the Mutton Chops Ghee Roast and as it sat in front of me my mouth was watering. Spice level on this was perfect, had a nice little kick but was really enjoyable and not in a overpowering way. I found that the chop may have been slightly overdone to my liking, however this didn't take the enjoyment away from it.

The meals ordered were enjoyed by everyone in the party which also included children (they really enjoyed the Prawns Garlic Butter). Pricing of the meals and overall was very reasonable and this place is worth a visit if you have never been. I will look to return here again if I visit Mumbai again.

featured_reviews.name: Kairo
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had lunch on Sunday. We were 5 people and it was an amazing experience. The food quality and taste both were top notch. We had order chicken and mutton thalis along with other dishes. We liked all of it. Especially Rucha ma'am was very friendly and asked us whether we like like our food. Tho service was a little slow, She was happy to help us and welcoming too.
Would recommend this place if ur fond of non veg food

featured_reviews.name: Hitesh Harisinghani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Nav Kayastha Pangat on a Sunday night and had a great experience. We waited around 10 minutes for a table, and the ambience along with the friendly staff made us feel comfortable right away. The warm Kokum drink is a perfect way to welcome guests!

What we ordered:

Mutton Kheema Pattice: A deep-fried snack with mutton kheema stuffed in mashed potato – absolutely delicious!

Bharleli Bombil: Bombil fish stuffed with green chutney and fried. Tasty, but next time I’d prefer plain bombil with chutney on the side.

Tisrya Kalwan: A unique and flavorful clams gravy that paired perfectly with wade.

The total bill for two came to ₹1400. Prices are on the higher side, but the menu is full of interesting and authentic CKP veg/non-veg dishes. Was this the best Mahrashtrian cuisine? No, not really but it's worth trying!

featured_reviews.name: Tejas takale
featured_reviews.review_text: I really liked the Kokum Sarbat welcome drink. We had the Chicken Thali, Surmai Thali, and Prawns Tawa Fry to start everything tasted great! 🍤
